title: Mesoscopic learning dynamics of extensive-width neural networks
authors: Shu Zhou, Jean Barbier, Sebastian Goldt
abstract: Understanding how stochastic gradient descent learns internal representations in wide neural networks trained on rich target functions is a central problem in machine learning. We study this question in two-layer neural networks learning target functions represented by networks of the same architecture, with arbitrary nonlinearity, and with network width and input dimension growing proportionally. In this regime, standard approaches for describing the learning dynamics require tracking a diverging number of overlaps, which measure correlations between learned and target features, leaving no obvious description in terms of a few order parameters. Here, we develop a mesoscopic description of learning by characterizing the distribution of overlaps. In the early stages of learning, we find that a Gaussian description of overlap statistics reduces the learning dynamics to a few collective variables that track learning of the target function's linear and quadratic components. We then estimate the timescale of specialization, when Gaussian closure breaks down and individual learned features begin to strongly correlate with specific target features. We find that specialization in extensive-rank networks is accelerated via a quadratic shielding mechanism, whereby learning the linear and quadratic components of the target function filters gradient fluctuations. We finally describe how the activation function determines the pattern of specialization and characterize the subsequent refinement of learned features. Together, these results show how collective learning gives way to individual feature discovery and clarify when learning in large neural networks admits a simple statistical description.
summary: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding learning dynamics in very wide neural networks. It moves beyond simple mean-field descriptions by characterizing the transition from collective learning to individual feature specialization. The key finding is the identification of a quadratic shielding mechanism that governs the timescale and nature of this feature discovery process.
main_problem: The paper investigates how Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) learns internal representations within wide neural networks trained on complex target functions.
main_result: It develops a mesoscopic description showing that learning proceeds through distinct stages: initial Gaussian-closure dynamics, followed by a specialization phase accelerated by a quadratic shielding mechanism, and finally, a refinement phase of feature discovery.
method: The analysis uses mean-field theory, expanding the activation function in Hermite polynomials, and deriving coupled Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) for mesoscopic overlap moments.
model_or_system: The model is a two-layer neural network trained via one-pass online SGD, comparing the student network's weights to a fixed teacher network in the extensive-width (proportional) limit.
key_observables: Overlaps ($\Omega_{ab}^{ij}$), mesoscopic overlap moments ($Q_{ab}^p$), and the population loss function ($L$).
important_parameters: Network width ($k$), input dimension ($d$), learning rate ($\eta$), and the degree of the Hermite polynomial expansion ($r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on the Gaussian-closure assumption in the early stages and the effective-confinement assumption when deriving dynamics in the specialized regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the four stages of learning (initialization, Gaussian-closure, specialization, refinement) and show the Mean-Square Displacement (MSD) of overlaps demonstrating a crossover in noise scaling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general problem in the extensive-width limit, deriving the initial dynamics using Gaussian closure, identifying the specialization transition driven by higher-order modes, and finally deriving closed equations for the refined dynamics exhibiting quadratic shielding.
why_interesting: The mathematical framework of deriving collective dynamics from microscopic correlations, especially the identification of shielding mechanisms that simplify complex noise structures, mirrors techniques used in analyzing quantum many-body systems near critical points or in disordered quantum magnets.
